coverage.instructions: Compare only the supplied original official fragment with the mapped CURRENT curated counterparts. Preserve actionable contracts, constraints, warnings, example intent and useful resource links; identifiers may be renamed to make examples valid. An explicit pinned-SDK/runtime-backed correction is valid curation, not a requirement to repeat an upstream mistake. Classify this fragment, not unrelated changes elsewhere in a whole guide. Headings/frontmatter/navigation alone are organizational.

criteria.covered: All substantive instructions in THIS source fragment are accurately retained.
criteria.organizational: This fragment is metadata, navigation or a heading with no missing substantive contract.
criteria.curated: A specific statement in THIS fragment is explicitly corrected or qualified by pinned implementation/runtime evidence.
criteria.gap: A substantive source contract is omitted or incorrectly replaced.
criteria.other: The supplied evidence cannot support a decision.

coverage.instructions: Does the supplied executable material teach the current TypeScript feature mechanism, typical use, meaningful consumer result and operational boundary? Shared setup is loaded selectively. External model/protocol I/O may be EXPLICITLY scripted while real public SDK algorithms execute. This does not establish provider/model quality. Do not require every optional configuration permutation. Pure navigation and non-TypeScript spelling/resource notes remain reference context, not fabricated TypeScript APIs. Missing concrete APIs are gaps.

criteria.complete: Real public SDK examples concretely demonstrate the feature with useful behavior and honest prerequisites/limits.
criteria.reference_context: The fragment is only navigation, conceptual taxonomy or non-TypeScript spelling/context; its runnable TypeScript counterpart is correctly routed.
criteria.partial: A concrete part of the TypeScript feature or essential prerequisite/boundary is missing.
criteria.gap: No real executable example implements the named TypeScript feature, or it substitutes an unsupported API.
criteria.other: The evidence is insufficient or contradictory.

correctness.instructions: Review ONLY the selected case and required helper declarations as teaching material. Shared infrastructure/guide excerpts are evidence, not duplicated case prose. Strict typecheck and actual shipping-runner result are observed. Check actual public APIs, useful invariants, fixture/live distinction, host effects, resource cleanup and exact version. Do not mistake explicitly scripted model/remote I/O for a replacement SDK. A successful fixture is not real model/provider quality proof.

criteria.correct: The actual SDK mechanism, consumer outcome and operational qualifications are supported.
criteria.mixed: A specific implementation/claim is unsupported or misleading despite other correct material.
criteria.incorrect: The core API, mechanism, outcome or safety claim is wrong.
criteria.other: The evidence cannot support a technical decision.

prose.instructions: Judge the selected instructional comments/title and progression together with the owning guide and shared setup. Code needed to exercise a real protocol is not verbose prose. Prefer concise Standard Technical English that tells unfamiliar agents what to import, why this mechanism, prerequisite and ownership limits. Do not demand reprinting shared setup in every case.

criteria.dense: Terse yet complete for the selected concept with the provided selective setup/guide.
criteria.verbose: Instructional prose repeats itself without a needed design/operational distinction.
criteria.incomplete: A necessary setup, conceptual transition or operational limit is missing.
criteria.other: The evidence cannot support a prose judgment.

route.instructions: Evaluate task discovery from actual master, index and owning reference to the selected real case. Design tasks start with architecture. Narrow implementation should not preload unrelated guides or the full corpus. CaseID discovery and shared setup may be one extra index hop.

criteria.correct: Relevant runnable material is discovered with clear setup and selective loading.
criteria.mixed: Some material is relevant but a needed route/stage is absent or unrelated preloading is required.
criteria.wrong: The route is missing, irrelevant or defeats progressive disclosure.
